transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I came in because I just can’t seem to get things in order anymore. My kitchen table is covered with papers—my husband’s appointment things, church flyers, notes from the senior center, little lists I start and don’t finish. I sit there trying to decide what to do first, and then… the whole day is gone.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

Yes… I suppose so. I’ve missed returning phone calls, and bills get left under piles of mail. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d do. And with my husband’s appointments… more than once I realized too late I never confirmed them.
Do you ever get confused about what day it is or where you are?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I know where I am. The day can slip by on me, but I’m not… lost like that.
Does this feel like a change from how organized and forgetful you used to be?

Yes… it does. I mean, I’ve never been perfect with papers, but it’s been causing real trouble for… about a year and a few months now. Since my husband started needing regular help with appointments and arrangements, mostly.
Do you feel these difficulties started because of the stress of managing your husband’s care?

I suppose the stress is part of it, yes. It’s been this much trouble for about a year and three months… around when my husband started needing regular help with his appointments and daily arrangements.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?
I… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say depressed exactly. Some days are harder than others, but I haven’t really thought of it that way.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?
I’m not sure I’d call it excessive. I do worry, yes… but many different things? I don’t know. Mostly I just try to get through what’s in front of me.
Have these difficulties been interfering with your day-to-day responsibilities?

Yes… it has. I had to step away from leading a big event at the senior center, which was embarrassing. And my daughter’s been checking over my bills and appointments now… she doesn’t really trust me to keep it all straight by myself anymore.
Have you been feeling sad most days?
I don’t think I’d say sad most days. I have quiet days, and I get frustrated… but sad, I’m not sure.
Even when you’re having a relatively calm day, do you still have the same trouble keeping track of things?

Yes… even on calm days. It’s like I sit at the kitchen table with all the papers—my husband’s appointments, church things, notes from the senior center, little lists I started—and I just… can’t seem to put them in order. I don’t know what to do first, and then the day slips away.
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?
Not really… I mean, I lose my train of thought sometimes, but I haven’t noticed trouble finding words exactly.
Do you ever get confused about the date or the month?
Not really… I mean, I might have to check the calendar, but I don’t think I get confused about the month.
Compared with a couple of years ago, do you feel your thinking and memory have clearly gotten worse?
I’m not sure I’d say clearly worse. I mean… some days feel harder, but I haven’t really kept track in a way that I could compare it to a couple years ago.
Have you made mistakes with medications, like missing doses or taking the wrong pills?

Not the wrong pills, I don’t think. I’ve missed things, though… calls I was supposed to return, bills left under mail, errands for my daughter. And I’ve realized too late I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments.
Do you feel your memory and organization are noticeably worse now than they used to be?

Yes… I think so. It’s mostly the organizing. I’ll sit at the kitchen table with all my husband’s appointment papers and church things and notes from the senior center, and lists I started… and I just can’t seem to figure out what to do first. Then the day’s gone.
Has your daughter told you that your memory or thinking has clearly gotten worse?

Yes… she has. Not in a mean way, but she’s started checking behind me with bills and appointments. I think she doesn’t really trust me to keep it all straight anymore. I also had to stop leading a big event at the senior center because it was just… too much to manage.
Has anyone besides your daughter noticed that your memory or thinking has gotten worse?
I’m not sure. No one’s really said it to me directly, besides my daughter. Maybe people have noticed, but… they haven’t told me.
During the past two weeks, have you felt down or depressed nearly every day?
I don’t know… not nearly every day, I don’t think. I get discouraged, but I wouldn’t say depressed every day.
Because of these memory and organization problems, do you now need help managing your bills?
Yes… my daughter has started looking over the bills, making sure I didn’t miss anything. I don’t love it, but I guess I do need the help now.
Do you often forget conversations or appointments even after someone has just told you about them?

Yes… I do. I’ve missed returning calls, and sometimes bills just sit under a stack of mail and I forget they’re there. I’ve forgotten errands I told my daughter I’d do, and… more than once I realized too late I never confirmed one of my husband’s appointments.
